newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific sets $2.2 bln spending plan.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific sets $2.2 bln spending plan.

text.p: Union Pacific Corp said Thursday it had approved a 1997 capital spending plan of $2.2 billion for Union Pacific Railroad, including more than $500 million to implement a merger with Southern Pacific Rail Corp.

It said the budget includes $615 million for 260 new locomotives and upgrade of existing units; $103 million for 1,023 new freight cars, including more than 500 new bi-level auto racks, and $1.0 billion for engineering projects, including 1,100 miles of rail and 3.4 million ties.
A high priority under the plan is the elimination of locomotive shortage at Southern Pacific, it said.

The plan also provides for connections to link systems of both railroads, and funds to begin rebuilding the Roseville Yard in Northern California, which will serve as the hub of the West Coast operations of the merged railroads, it said.

Union Pacific said it will start a $750 million project to upgrage and add capacity to key corriders, including Southern Pacific's Sunset Route between El Paso and Los Angeles, the Tucumcari Route between Kansas City and El Paso, and Union Pacific's Kansas Pacific line between Denver and Topeka.
The company said it expects the corridor projects to be one of its highest priorities in 1998, when it can begin to take advantage of labor agreements being negotiated now.
More than $50 million will be spent in 1997 to develop computer and inforation systems to prepare for the upgrades, it said.
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Dick Davidson said that while train performance and locomotive availability are improving, recent flooding in the West has caused problems.
He said the company would not allow a lapse in service while implementing improvements.
